question: Should review-required Policy doctor repairs be exposed through generic Doctor `changes` output even though no config is applied, including for `tools.alsoAllow` permission guidance?
rationale: The code is plausible and proven, but the output contract and permission guidance affect operator expectations, automation parsing, and security-boundary wording in a way automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Use `changes` for skipped previews
options.body: Keep the PR shape, with docs and proof making the skipped/non-applied state explicit, after the base preview stack is refreshed.

options.title: Use a separate preview channel
options.body: Move review-required preview text out of generic `changes` so that channel remains reserved for applied repairs.

options.title: Hold the permission-preview slice
options.body: Pause or close this slice if maintainers do not want Doctor suggesting manual `tools.alsoAllow` grants or removals from policy findings.

recommendation.title: Use `changes` for skipped previews
recommendation.body: Keep the PR shape, with docs and proof making the skipped/non-applied state explicit, after the base preview stack is refreshed.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent Policy doctor repair behavior and own the open stacked preview changes being reviewed here.
